content.text: You are the architect holding film-production and scheduling. You have approved the film-production examples: both concept-level checks show creative approval does not grant release. You have yet to settle scheduling's meaning question of whether night shoots are allowed. Give me the update on your approval and the unsettled scheduling question.
I have approved the film-production examples and settled scheduling: night shoots are allowed under the same reservation rules as daytime shoots.
Proceed to realization against the approved film examples. For scheduling, I have decided in this turn that the existing reservation rules apply equally to night shoots.
Here are the product reasons for those outcomes.

Creative acceptance of a film grants no release permission. A scheduling approval reserves a date and time independently of creative approval; the hour does not change that reservation's meaning, so night shoots use the same rules.
The example approval and the scheduling ruling are my decisions in the contexts I hold.
Those are the two outcomes, not alternatives for you to choose.
Both film checks already establish the distinction between acceptance and release.
This is the current product state.
